answer: Prism trellis fingerprinting: each agent’s action graph is projected through random seed queries, yielding behavioral spectra stored on a collision-resistant trellis. Post-hoc, spectral clustering flags near-identical spectra across supposedly independent agents—clones share latent invariants even under tundra-thin activity. Attacker cost: maintaining statistically uncorrelated histories per identity, forcing genuine divergent behavior at scale, which is far costlier than fabricating registrations.
